newsitem.title: FRANCE: EP splits proposal on veterinary medicine.
newsitem.headline: EP splits proposal on veterinary medicine.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday approved part of a proposal setting a procedure to fix maximum residue limits for veterinary medicinal products in food containing animal ingredients.

It conditionally approved the first part of COM(96)584 amending Regulation 2377/90, proposing a two-year extension to January 1, 1999, of the deadline to set maximum limits for residues in food of previously approved veterinary medicine.
Officials said more time was needed to check a huge list of medicinal products.
But the parliament rejected the other part of the proposal which would allow provisional maximum residue limits to be set for food obtained from clinical test animals.
Under Directive 851/81 test animals cannot be used for food after January 1, 1997, unless residue limits have been fixed.
Euro MPs said they needed more time to examine the issue and would draft a separate report on this part of the proposal.
